themes.title: Sovereign AI courts capital: Humain IPO, G42 US equity
themes.summary: Saudi Arabia's PIF-backed Humain is staffing an IPO preparation team barely 16 months after launch, while Abu Dhabi's G42 is reportedly weighing a US majority shareholder to secure chip access. Gulf AI champions are moving off state balance-sheets toward global capital markets, and export-control gravity is now bending Gulf equity structures themselves.
themes.angle: Gulf sovereign AI is trading state ownership for market access - watch the cap-table math on chips.

themes.title: The AI slowdown debate: brakes vs the AGI sprint
themes.summary: OpenAI's chief scientist publicly urged 'extreme caution' and predicted labs will voluntarily slow development, landing the safety-vs-speed debate on front pages just as WSJ declares the AGI era open and Jensen Huang reportedly stakes an AGI claim. Executives now face two competing narratives on AI velocity - with capex commitments as the collateral.
themes.angle: The pacing debate is now a board decision: voluntary slowdown vs giga-project velocity.

themes.title: Deals, listings and the AI funding cycle
themes.summary: Anthropic walked away from a roughly $6B Decart acquisition, drone maker UForce is raising at about $5B, and AI-infrastructure listings (Longsys in Hong Kong, Preferred Networks in Japan) test investor appetite. FT flags the macro risk: US long-term rates decisively above 5% could derail the AI boom.
themes.angle: AI dealflow is bifurcating: acquirers walk, infrastructure listings carry the cycle.
